title: Transport of the trace formula to the non-finite stages
statement:
Fix the coefficient setup of [sk-d-setup], in particular a prime $\ell\ne p$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let the coefficient ring range over the three non-finite stages

$$
\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,\ E,\ \overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\},
$$

the $\mathcal O_E$-stage being the normalized systems of
finite-level objects, the $E$-stage its
rationalization, and the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-stage the colimit over
finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0/\mathbf F_q$ be separated of finite
type and let $K$ be a Weil datum with coefficients in
$\Lambda$, that is, a Weil pair at the stage $\Lambda$ in the all-stage
sense of [sk-def-sf-weil-complexes]: at $\mathcal O_E$ a normalized system
of finite-level Weil pairs ([sk-d-weil]) whose transitions commute with the
$\varphi_n$ (a compatible tower of Weil pairs as in
[def-trf-adic-system]), and at $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ its
rationalization and colimit. At the field stages the underlying coefficient category is rationalized first, and the Weil isomorphism is taken in that category as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]; an invertible integral lift on a lattice is not required. Then:

1. **(a)** *Trace identity.* The identity of
[thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-finite-ring] holds for every $m\ge1$ with $A$ replaced by
$\Lambda$, with compact cohomology and
traces taken at the stage $\Lambda$: at $\mathcal O_E$ this is the trace of an endomorphism of a perfect complex ([sk-d-trace]), and at the field stages it is the alternating sum of ordinary traces on cohomology. The coefficient categories and compact cohomology are those of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]; field-stage Weil pairs are understood as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].
1. **(b)** *Euler-product form.* Let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, write $e_x$ for the degree of
a closed point $x\in|X_0|$, and put
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{x\in|X_0|}
\det\bigl(1-T^{e_x}F_x\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)^{-1}
\in1+T\Lambda[[T]],
$$
a locally finite product. For a complex, the stalk determinant denotes
the alternating product of the determinants on its cohomology. Then
$$
L(X_0,K,T)=\prod_{i}
\det\bigl(1-TF\mid H_c^i(X,K)\bigr)^{(-1)^{i+1}}
$$
as formal power series, the product being finite; if $X_0$ is a curve and $K$ is a sheaf in degree zero, it
runs over $0\le i\le2$. Any field embedding
$\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\to\mathbf C$ carries the identity to one
in $\mathbf C[[T]]$.

proof.text: Finite-level hypotheses. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$, and let $K_n$ be a level of the normalized system (or a reduction of an integral representative at a field stage). For the given integral Weil system, $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ is part of [def-trf-adic-system]. For an integral representative at a field stage, [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] gives bounded constructible reductions, and [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] gives their normalization $K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_1\simeq K_1$. These reductions also have finite Tor amplitude in the sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], that is, for every sheaf $M$ of $A_n$-modules: filter $M$ by the subsheaves $\varpi^iM$, $0\le i\le n$; each successive quotient $Q$ is a sheaf of $A_1$-modules, and $K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}Q\simeq(K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_1)\otimes^L_{A_1}Q\simeq K_1\otimes_{A_1}Q$, where tensoring over the constant field $A_1$ is exact (sectionwise vector spaces, then exact sheafification), so its cohomology sheaves are $\mathcal H^r(K_1)\otimes_{A_1}Q$ and vanish outside the fixed range $[r_0,s_0]$ of $K_1$. The $n$ filtration triangles give the same interval $[r_0,s_0]$ for $K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}M$, proving the required Tor bound. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) it has an etale-origin witness. Choose a compactification of $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_q$ by [thm-nagata-compactification] and base change it to $k$. The admissibility in the finite trace statements is the constructible condition of [def-trf-admissibility], whose statement explicitly asserts that every separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes satisfies it. Thus it applies to the structure morphisms, graphs and fixed-point base changes on this compactification, at every $A_n$; no unrestricted ambient exceptional adjoint is being assumed. These observations discharge the geometric finite-level hypotheses wherever the following steps use them.

source.place: Step 1: the finite-level hypotheses; the constructible admissibility convention

proof.text:
Finite identities, including noninvertible coefficients. For any $K_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ and any Frobenius coefficient map $\psi_n:L\Phi^*K_n\to K_n$, apply [thm-trf-coefficient-morphism-trace-formula] with the witnesses and compactification of Step 1. For every $m\ge1$ it gives
$$\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(F_{c,m}(\psi_n)\mid R\Gamma_c(X,K_n))=\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\operatorname{tr}_{A_n}(\psi_{n,m,\bar y}\mid K_{n,\bar y}).$$
The fixed-point set is finite by [thm-trf-frobenius-fixed-points]. The result applies to the invertible maps of the given integral Weil system and also to the possibly noninvertible reductions of a denominator-cleared field-stage map.

source.place: Step 1: apply the finite formula also to Frobenius coefficient morphisms

proof.text: Compatibility and perfect realizations. Write $P_n=R\Gamma_c(X,K_n)$ and $P_{\bar y,n}=K_{n,\bar y}$. Apply [thm-trf-finite-coefficient-map] to $A_{n+1}\to A_n$: the compact-support and pullback comparisons identify their reductions with $P_n$ and $P_{\bar y,n}$, respectively, and carry the finite-level trace to its reduction. More precisely, [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems](1),(3) says that both towers are normalized perfect towers and that, for each fixed $m$, their global and local operators are compatible. Its clause (2) gives bounded finite-free $\mathcal O_E$ realizations $P_{\mathcal O}$ and $P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}$, reduction isomorphisms $P_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L A_n\simeq P_n$ and $P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}\otimes^L A_n\simeq P_{\bar y,n}$, and lifts of the compatible operators. Its clause (4) identifies the reduction of each realized trace with the corresponding finite trace. In particular the integral realizations have one bounded finite-free model, as required for the unit's Step 3.

source.place: Steps 2–3: coefficient comparison, normalized perfect towers, realization and trace reduction

proof.text:
Integral trace identity. For a fixed $m\ge1$, let $V_m$ and $V_{y,m}$ be lifts of the global and local families of Step 3, and put
$$\delta_m=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_m\mid P_{\mathcal O})-\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal O_E}(V_{y,m}\mid P_{\bar y,\mathcal O}).$$
By [prop-trf-adic-coefficient-morphism-systems](4), reduction of $\delta_m$ modulo $\varpi^n$ is the difference of the two sides of Step 2, so is zero for every $n$. The same clause identifies $\mathcal O_E$ with $\varprojlim_n A_n$; hence $\delta_m=0$. In the given Weil system these lifts are its realized Frobenius operators, and the clause also says that the traces are independent of the lift. This proves (a) at $\mathcal O_E$, and proves the integral identity for compatible coefficient maps needed for rationalization.

source.place: Step 3: pass the finite equalities to the separated complete coefficient ring

proof.text:
The $E$ stage. Apply [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] to the underlying $E$ object and its Weil isomorphism. A lattice exists by the explicit object convention in that theorem, and its only additional hypotheses are precisely the finite-level etale-origin and compactification conditions discharged in Step 1. Thus the theorem applies without assuming an integral Weil isomorphism. Its finiteness clause gives bounded finite-dimensional global and stalk cohomology. For clarity, its denominator statement implements the unit's Step 4 as follows: for $\varphi_E=\varpi^{-N}u$, the integral-model statement [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model](3),(4) identifies the operators with
$$F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}(U_m\otimes E),\qquad F_{y,m}=\varpi^{-Nm}(U_{y,m}\otimes E).$$
Each iterate contains exactly $m$ copies of the one-step coefficient map, so the exponent is $Nm$. On the bounded finite-free models of Step 3, [lem-trf-chain-supertrace](c) computes the integral trace as the alternating sum of the diagonal matrix entries of a chain representative. Applying $\mathcal O_E\to E$ to these entries commutes with this finite sum, so it gives the trace of the scalar-extended chain map. The field-supertrace clause of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws] then identifies it with the alternating ordinary traces on cohomology. Multiply the integral equality of Step 4 by $\varpi^{-Nm}$ to obtain the required equality. No invertibility of $u$ on the lattice is required. The theorem supplies these constructions for a general field-stage input and gives (a) over $E$.

The common $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ stage. The field-stage Weil pair is represented over a finite $E$ as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. If its isomorphism and its inverse are initially represented over different fields, choose a common finite overfield at which both inverse identities hold; this is exactly equality in the displayed filtered Hom colimit of the first definition. Apply [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] to that $E$-Weil pair: its finite-level hypotheses were discharged in Step 1. Its statement says that global cohomology, stalks and Frobenius operators are scalar extensions of the $E$-stage data, that the traces are the images of the $E$ traces, and that the identity is independent of the representative and common overfield. This proves (a) at the last stage, with finite-dimensional cohomology in finitely many degrees.

source.place: Step 4: finite coefficient field of definition and common-stage scalar extension

proof.text: Euler product and the curve range. Apply the existing node [thm-trf-l-function-euler-product] to the Weil pair over $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Its hypotheses are those of [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] or [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar], respectively, already verified in Steps 1, 5 and 6. Its definitions use the same global operator $F=F_{c,K}^{\,1}$, the same one-circuit closed-point operator $F_x$ up to conjugation, and the alternating stalk determinant. Clause (1) gives coefficientwise local finiteness and constant term $1$, clause (2) gives the finite alternating product over compact cohomology, and clause (3) gives $H_c^i=0$ outside $\{0,1,2\}$ when $\dim X_0\le1$ and $K$ is a sheaf. These are exactly every assertion in (b) before the embedding.

source.place: Step 5: the existing Euler-product subnode realizes the determinant argument, finiteness and curve bound

proof.text: Embedding. For a ring homomorphism $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\to\mathbf C$, the coefficientwise map on formal series respects addition and multiplication: in degree $N$ the product coefficient is the finite sum $\sum_{r=0}^N a_rb_{N-r}$. It respects inverses of series of constant term $1$ by applying it to $ff^{-1}=1$, and respects determinants because they are finite signed sums of products of matrix entries. In each degree the locally finite Euler product of Step 7 is a finite product, so its image is the corresponding Euler product of the images. Apply this coefficient map to the equality of Step 7. This proves the final embedding assertion without any continuity or analytic convergence assumption on $\iota$.

source.place: Step 6: coefficientwise application of the field embedding

proof_origin.place: Steps 1–6, expanded using the existing statement-bearing subnodes of the same unit and the coefficient-transport units
